name: Ensemble
reason: Take the authored intent/response split and explainable influence-rule idea. Existing YAIRPG handles directed state, legal actions, funding, clock and durable publication. A dependency would duplicate these owners while still requiring private knowledge, consent, seed and atomicity adapters.
strongest_gap: An authored social bid, independent recipient stance and knowledge-visible outcome consumer, using the already implemented directed axes/causes/controllers/Ink.

evidence.claim: Directed scalar closeness/attraction default to0, clamp0–100; temporary moods last3 turns and event labels last only the current turn.
Rule bindings are enumerated against a shared social record; matched intent weights accumulate and retain rule explanations.
Acceptance reads the reverse actor pair for the same category/type/intent, rejects negative weight, and accepts by default if no reverse match exists.
Action traversal checks condition bindings and accept/reject polarity, computes influence, and excludes negative-scoring terminals.
getActions takes intent scores and computed reverse acceptance, then sorts and binds terminals.
doAction directly applies the returned bound effects; this function does not recheck prerequisites, stale state, cost budgets, or perform durable publication.
Accepted notes add10 closeness each direction; rejected notes add10 only to the initiator and emit a directed romantic-failure event. No money, item or effort cost is specified.
A romantic-failure trigger adds10 from the recipient toward another distinct character without a witnessing/knowledge prerequisite.
Triggers set effects into current shared socialRecord and intentionally retain offstage characters for perfect information, excluding eliminated characters.
Schema-defined numeric effects apply arithmetic/clamping; only reciprocal categories automatically mirror the reverse relation.
Timestep advancement copies nonzero-duration facts, drops duration0 events, and decrements booleans, expiring them to false.
The example renders hero choices, commits a clicked action, runs triggers, shows accept/refusal text, rereads relationships, and dispatches the next turn.
The example checks relationship-based endings, advances one timestep, and recalculates choices. It does not autonomously commit NPC actions in this loop.
Best role bindings are selected with Underscore random, with no passed seeded RNG.
The intended package is a singleton bundled with Underscore and internal state modules.
Action parsing calls validate.action, but that validator is a TODO stub returning its input.
BSD-4-Clause UC-specific license requires source/binary notices and an acknowledgement in advertising mentioning features/use; no university endorsement.
Initial history specifies actor-role traits and hero strength0/intelligence5, with closeness left at the schema default.
Hero toward love has a20 base increase-closeness intent; love toward hero gets-10; positive existing closeness contributes5.
Condition evaluation supports time windows/order and queries global socialRecord; no observer/knowledge holder is an API parameter here.
Public copy/history APIs can move social record data but do not provide the YAIRPG envelope/atomic publisher.
Rule matching recursively binds distinct cast members, so work scales with rule arity and cast size. No performance measurement is claimed.
getAction stops on the first intent with an available action, then selects its best terminal. This is narrower than globally maximizing action scores across all intents.
Directed/reciprocal/undirected schema terminology describes separate single-person, asymmetric pair and automatically symmetric pair state.

trace.prerequisite: Schema and cast/history/rules/actions loaded. Authored traits make hero want increasing closeness to love while the reverse increase intent is negative. No item/money/time budget condition exists in this action path.
trace.decision: getActions traverses RAISECLOSENESS -> WRITELOVENOTE -> terminal picked by reverse-intent acceptance. Player chooses the already-bound rejection action shown as Write Love Note <REJECT>. Engine does not make a second interactive responder decision on click.
trace.cost: No material, currency, stamina or paid duration; opportunity cost is one player turn. This is absence of cost in this example path, not a claim that Ensemble cannot represent resources as custom predicates.
trace.mutations: Rejected note increments only initiator->responder closeness by10 and sets romantic-failure initiator->responder true. Shared record clamps numerical range.
trace.consumer: Immediate trigger binds would-be lover/recipient/other distinct actor, checks absence of other->recipient failure, increments recipient->other closeness10. The UI reads directed closeness and attraction, and closeness drives placement and >=90 ending checks.
trace.aftermath: Next turn copies closeness, omits duration0 failure event, and recalculates social volitions. Numeric initial20/-10 and rejection-driven love->rival10 are static derivations only; no run/benchmark/browser proof.

fit.directed_friendship: Good representational fit via directed numeric/boolean predicates; terms and relationship dynamics are author-defined, not built-in friendship progression.
fit.romance: Can represent asymmetric attraction and accepted/rejected terminals; example’s general closeness threshold/default acceptance is insufficient for action-specific mutual willingness and enduring agreements.
fit.rivalry: Can represent asymmetric friction/competition and third-party outcomes, but the sample’s global rival boost is not knowledge-bounded.
fit.independent_goals: Rules score per pair and self-directed attribute desires. Runtime scheduling and multi-step persistent goal pursuit belong to the host; bundled example performs hero actions only.
fit.knowledge: Shared socialRecord evaluation and perfect-information triggers provide no demonstrated per-actor epistemic enforcement in inspected path. YAIRPG must explicitly allowlist own knowledge plus public facts; filtering cast alone is insufficient.

integration.proposed: An authored bounded rule scorer consumes only the acting person’s knowledge/basis, own directed memories/axes, and declared personal goal evidence, then returns a registered command ID, target ID and expected sequence. Do not pass the full simulationFacts object: it includes engine truth for legal validation, not an omniscience-safe motive context. Current authoritative command previews/commit rechecks alone inspect actual funding, stock, custody, bodies, locations, consent/support and costs/effects. A recipient independently reads its own stance; only its explicitly delivered answer becomes initiator knowledge. Existing Ink can present the result.
must_keep: inspectActorChoices/acceptActorProposal contract; never send Ensemble effects as authoritative proposal
Current directed knowledge/relationship records with cause receipts
One common-clock scheduler and current native durable publication
Optional additive definitions and explicit old-save compatibility; no automatic enrollment/history
missing_consumers: One authored invitation/cooperation/competition bid over already implemented legal command candidates
An independent authored recipient stance that can accept, refuse or defer without trust forcing romance
An observed reply/aftermath scene that changes only declared directed axes/memories and knowledge recipients

risks.detail: Singleton socialRecord and cached main volitions can mutate outside the cloned YAIRPG plan. History import/export does not synchronize actor axes, causes, native inventory, seed or envelope transaction. Do not persist an independent authoritative social graph.
Reverse-intent no-match default is accept; trigger engine explicitly retains perfect information. Add explicit willingness and actor-observed prerequisites rather than copying defaults.
Underscore random selects ties and every setupNextTimeStep clones state; chronological turns are not YAIRPG played minutes. Avoid calling it per minute or letting recalculation alter durable choices.

Current default HEAD is2019, latest release2019 despite repository pushed_at2022 and archived false. JSON domain needs schema/cast/history/rules/action grammar; validator action is a TODO stub. Wiki global-best getAction description is broader than its inspected first-nonempty-intent implementation. No current community-maintenance or package-security assurance.
Pair matrix, distinct-role binding recursion and history copying suggest growth costs; no timings/cast-scale benchmark performed.

UC-specific BSD4 includes advertising acknowledgement and notice retention, unlike common BSD3; vendored Underscore1.8.2 has an MIT header. Conceptual original adaptation copies no code/assets/domain text. Any later source adoption must preserve applicable notices and review advertising requirement.

trial.title: A route invitation with an independent work priority
trial.scope: One opt-in home-world scene using two explicitly adult original actor templates, one existing finite work site, one invitation situation, and existing registered commands. Names, identities, numbers and dialogue remain director-review proposals.
prerequisites: Actors have met through actual observation, are alive/in the same supported world and location, and the invitation is known to the initiator.
Responder has an authored own goal: complete a funded route-report shift before a social meeting. A private, explicitly authored willingness flag controls whether romance is an available offer.
player_choices: Invite for a friendly three-minute route walk; separately express romantic interest only through an authored, available respectful offer.
Offer cooperation on the actual funded shift or compete openly for its finite work claim; decline or defer the scene.
trial.decision_rule: Score motives using only actor-known evidence/basis, the actor’s own directed memories/axes and its declared personal goal. Select only legal command IDs from inspectActorChoices; do not use eligibility reasons or full simulationFacts as motives, because they can encode hidden engine truth. Evaluate the responder independently in its private stance context. Authoritative previews/commits separately enforce true funding, location/life/contact, participant capacity and support. Being free or earning trust does not imply romantic consent. Missing willingness means no romance offer. Only a delivered answer reveals that answer; private scores never become player-facing diagnostics.

costs.invitation: Three played minutes of the initiator’s scheduled time; no money or material cost and no acceptance purchase. If no meeting occurs, only the disclosed invitation effort is spent.
costs.accepted_meeting: Reserve both participants for the same three-minute job; use the one common clock.
costs.work: Use a real funded site and exact native/simulation stock and budget, with published costs/refund policy rather than score-based fabricated supply.

trial.mutations: One cause-scoped directed memory records accepted/declined/deferred. Friendship reliability can change in only the authored direction. Attraction and rivalry are distinct axes; romantic agreement is an explicit two-person situation/commitment. A refusal does not impose automatic reputation or attraction punishment. Unknown observers gain no knowledge.
trial.downstream: A later local meeting uses the saved accepted plan or respectful refusal memory; the NPC first continues its funded work at its controller boundary. A heard report reveals only the result delivered, not the other actor’s private goal score.
trial.failure: Stale proposal, missing funds/stock/contact/life or busy participants reject at existing gates. A lost completion prerequisite uses explicit completionSupport and the declared refund/forfeit policy. No accepted partnership, intimacy, XP or items are granted by a failed invitation.

acceptance_criteria.check: Generate two actor-local projections with an unobserved report known only to one.
acceptance_criteria.pass: The other actor cannot choose based on it; an actual delivered report changes only its legal informed choice. Public UI exposes no hidden score.

acceptance_criteria.check: Compare friendship, romantic and work/rival options with asymmetric state and explicit consent false/true.
acceptance_criteria.pass: High trust alone cannot create romance; refusal is distinct, respected and remembered; reverse axes remain independently authored.

acceptance_criteria.check: Schedule NPC funded work while player chooses another activity, then invite while busy and after completion.
acceptance_criteria.pass: NPC acts at one existing clock boundary, pays actual costs, completes once and can defer social contact. No browser-closed time is invented.

acceptance_criteria.check: Change sequence, remove stock or contact, and replay a cause.
acceptance_criteria.pass: Existing proposal gates reject stale/illegal commitments; causes cannot farm relationship effects; no duplicate items/work/rewards or second scheduler appear.

acceptance_criteria.check: Later, under an authorized gameplay/save gate, use generated opt-in and old unenrolled saves on an isolated origin, including failed write/reload.
acceptance_criteria.pass: Current envelope/native publication preserves invitation, separate memories and job exactly once; failed persistence publishes nothing; old saves gain no enrollment or history.

trial.implementation_boundary: Builder/integrator-owned future work only. No runtime implementation, new state publisher, engine switch, tests or dependency adoption is selected by this research.

depth_map.source_fact: Directed scalar axes can diverge from temporary booleans and duration0 event labels; reciprocal mirroring is a schema operation, not a negotiated agreement.
depth_map.incumbent_implication: Keep attraction, reliability, grievance, promises, current mood and actor-observed event knowledge in their distinct existing owners. Do not normalize YAIRPG arbitrary finite axes to the sample0–100 range.

depth_map.source_fact: Offstage and eliminated actors are excluded from volition effects, while offstage actors remain eligible for trigger effects. Both evaluators query the shared record.
depth_map.incumbent_implication: Offscreen social aftermath, institutions and rumors need actual observation/report/access channels. Cast filtering alone cannot prevent use of global private truth. Known obligations can affect motives without exposing hidden compliance.

depth_map.source_fact: runRules iterates stored rules/bindings and trigger process sets effects immediately. Later conditions can see earlier writes. This is a sequential pass, not a demonstrated fixed-point solver, and no cause-based repeat receipt is checked in the trigger path.
depth_map.incumbent_implication: A social event -> rumor -> faction stance -> access consequence chain requires authored ordering and existing cause receipts. Repeated trigger evaluation cannot be treated as a free idempotent query.

depth_map.source_fact: Current duration0 labels vanish on advancement while previous history remains queryable through relative windows. Ordered conditions update a last-match time; source comments identify unresolved multi-match behavior. Boolean expiry writes false, not an arbitrary schema default. Calling an earlier timestep clears later social history only.
depth_map.incumbent_implication: A mood expiring is not forgiveness or deletion of memory; a previously heard betrayal can have later consequences. Existing YAIRPG played clock/retained evidence/branch owners govern timing. Raw socialRecord rewind is not body/stock/job/native-save reversal. Ordered-history semantics need a later targeted check before adopting code.
depth_map.status: source-demonstrated; exception behavior unexecuted; original implication

depth_map.source_fact: Self-directed desires and action-influence weights support learning/work motives, but the example loops only player hero commits; position and ending are explicit consumers of the same social axes.
depth_map.incumbent_implication: NPC work, social meetings and competition can share real sites/funds/participant time and still produce different scenes, access or campaign endings. The existing scheduler and Ink present those authored downstream choices. No planner, complete persistent-goal system or universal social score is established by the example.
